scenes.text: Your browser’s secret handshake nobody sees
scenes.subtext: How a tiny text query finds the whole internet
scenes.narration: Ever wonder how typing example.com magically loads a site? It’s not magic, it’s DNS whispering behind the scenes. Stick around, we’ll expose the hidden handshake.

scenes.title: DNS Query Journey
scenes.narration: First, your laptop shouts a query to the recursive resolver. The resolver asks the root server, which points to the TLD server. That TLD server then points to the authoritative server, which finally drops the IP address back down. Each hop is a polite ask, not a brute‑force scan. And that’s why a single lookup takes milliseconds, not seconds.

scenes.label: Average DNS lookup time
scenes.context: Fast enough to feel instant, but every millisecond adds up across the web.
scenes.narration: On average, a DNS lookup costs about 97 milliseconds. That’s a blink, but multiply it by billions of requests, and you see why DNS performance matters. Faster lookups = smoother browsing.
